read.sections.0.text.back: Most cities began as small places. A small town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a harbour, a railway line or a factory. Better transport also helps, because people and goods can go in and out more easily. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold-storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the capital. That created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to work there. A change like this is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.
read.sections.0.text.source: Most cities start small. A town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a harbour, a railway or factories. Better transport also helps, because it lets people and goods move in and out more easily. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold-storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the capital city. That created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to do them. This kind of change is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: Most cities started small. A city can grow if there are new jobs. A harbour, a train or a factory can bring jobs. Good transport helps people and goods move. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road opened. A big cold room also opened. That room keeps fish fresh. This made 800 new jobs. People moved to Bayview to work. This is called urbanisation. More and more people live in cities.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: Most cities start small. A town can grow when new jobs come. A harbour, a railway or factories can bring jobs. Good transport helps people and goods move. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road opened. A big cold room opened too. It kept fish fresh. This made 800 new jobs. People moved to Bayview for the jobs. This is called urbanisation. More people live in towns and cities.

read.sections.1.heading.back: Real cities grow in similar ways
read.sections.1.heading.source: Real cities grew in similar ways

read.sections.1.text.back: Many real cities grew in similar ways. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stopping place on a new railway line. Workers and traders came, and the stopping place grew into a city. Shenzhen, in southern China, was a small town with about 30,000 residents in 1980. Then the government made it a special area for business. Factories opened, and millions of people moved there to work. Now Shenzhen is one of the biggest cities in China. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population grow.
read.sections.1.text.source: Many real cities grew in a similar way. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stop on a new railway. Workers and traders came, and the stop grew into a city. Shenzhen, in southern China, was a small city of about 30,000 people in 1980. Then the government made it a special area for business. Factories opened, and millions of people moved there for work. Today it is one of the biggest cities in China. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population grow.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Real cities also grow like this. Nairobi is a big city in Kenya. This city started in 1899 as a railway station. Workers and traders came. The station grew into a city. Shenzhen is a city in China. In 1980, this city was still small. Then many factories opened there. Millions of people came to work. Now this city is one of the biggest cities in China. In both places, jobs and transport made the population grow.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: Real cities grew like this too. Nairobi is a big city in Kenya. It started in 1899 as a stop on a railway. Workers and traders came. The stop grew into a city. Shenzhen is a city in China. In 1980, it was small. Then many factories opened there. Millions of people came to work. Now it is one of China's biggest cities. In both places, jobs and transport made the population grow.

read.sections.2.heading.note: 'Pressures' (strain on a growing city) rendered as 'beban' (burden) here and in the write prompt, sentence starter, self-check and speaking task. 'Tekanan' is the literal word but read awkwardly ('satu tekanannya adalah ...').

read.sections.2.text.back: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more houses, clean water and health services. Services are help that people need, such as a clinic or a school. Infrastructure is the basic systems a place needs, such as roads, water pipes and electric cables. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview had new houses, a school and bus routes. But people waited a long time at the only clinic, because the clinic did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners pay attention to burdens like this and make plans from the start.
read.sections.2.text.source: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more homes, clean water and health care. A service is help that people need, like a clinic or a school. Infrastructure means the basic systems a place needs, such as roads, water pipes and power lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview has new houses, a school and bus routes. But people wait a long time at the only clinic, because it did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners watch for pressures like this and plan ahead.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Growth can be good. A big city has more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need houses and clean water. They need services such as clinics. They need infrastructure, such as roads and pipes. All of this takes time to build. In Year 15, people waited a long time at the Bayview clinic. The clinic did not grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems from the start.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Growth can be good. A big city has more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need homes and clean water. They need a service like a clinic. They need infrastructure, like roads and pipes. These take time to build. In Year 15, people wait a long time at the Bayview clinic. It did not grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems early.

watch.summary.back: This video starts with a fact: today, more than half of humans live in cities. About 10,000 years ago, humans started farming. They could grow food, so they settled in villages. Later, better ways of farming produced extra food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other work. Villages grew into cities. Trade also grew, with carts, ships, roads and harbours. Much later, factories and new machines helped cities grow even bigger. Cities added police, firefighters, roads and ways to get rid of rubbish. In the future, more and more people will live in cities. The video says that cities must provide enough food, toilets and schools for everyone. Cities must also look after nature. Some ideas are rooftop gardens, tall buildings, and electricity from the sun and wind.
watch.summary.source: The video starts with a fact: today, more than half of all people live in towns and cities. About 10,000 years ago, people began to farm. They could grow food, so they stayed in villages. Later, better farming made extra food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other jobs. Villages grew into cities. Trade grew too, with carts, ships, roads and ports. Much later, factories and new machines helped cities grow even bigger. Cities added police, fire services, roads and ways to take away waste. In the future, even more people will live in cities. The video says cities must give everyone enough food, toilets and schools. They must also protect the land. Ideas include rooftop gardens, tall buildings, and power from the sun and wind.
